caption: Front door — pick the kind of flash sale in plain words, or describe it in one line.
Ideas from your sales — the blank page becomes “pick a smart idea,” each tied to a real number.
What’s on sale — the new part: pick many products at once (a section, your best sellers, or one by one).
The discount — set one percent; the wizard does the math for every product and flags any that would not really be cheaper.
When & how many — plain timing (“this weekend”), an optional stock cap, and the coupon-stacking choice in plain words.
Review — the real shopper card, a one-line summary, plain heads-up, then save a draft, schedule it, or turn it on.
The smart heads-up — reads your live sales and coupons and says, in plain words, what gets replaced, what stacks, what resets, what is skipped.
What the shopper sees — the flash card already exists: badge, struck-through price, live countdown, and a stock bar.
